post.contentHtml:
Backlog Is Up, So Why Did the Stock Fall?

Aebi Schmidt Holding (NASDAQ: AEBI), a Swiss-based maker of snow removal, sweeping and specialty vehicle equipment, reported its Q3 2026 results on November 11. Revenue, profit and backlog all rose, but the company lowered its full-year guidance (the earnings outlook a company provides), and the stock closed down about 4.25% on the day of the announcement. This article focuses on these mixed signals.

Q3 Numbers at a Glance

ItemQ3 2026Year over year
Net revenueAbout $493 million+4.6%
Adjusted EBITDAAbout $44.2 million+4.9% (margin 9.0%, unchanged)
Net incomeAbout $10.8 millionAbout $1.2 million a year earlier
New ordersAbout $528 million+2.0%
BacklogAbout $1.3 billion+16.4%
Net debtAbout $446 million-4.8%

Adjusted EBITDA is operating profit before interest, taxes and depreciation, with one-time items removed. It is used to gauge the cash-generating power of the core business. Positives include the sharp rise in net income, lower net debt, and leverage (the ratio of debt to earnings) falling from 3.24x a year ago to 2.66x.

Where the Market Was Disappointed: Lower Guidance

  • Full-year net revenue outlook: $1.95–2.15 billion → $1.95–2.00 billion (upper end cut)
  • Full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook: $175–195 million → $170–180 million
  • Year-end leverage target: around 2.0x → below 2.5x (including payment for a planned acquisition)

According to some media outlets, revenue fell short of market expectations. Consensus figures vary by data provider, so the exact gap is hard to pin down.

Cost Pressure Weighing on Margins

The company cited high inflationary pressure. Gross margin in Q3 was 19.2%, down 0.8 percentage points. The explanation is that costs rose first, while price increases took effect later than expected. Supply chain disruptions and weaker demand in China and the Middle East were also named as burdens. Revenue in Europe and other regions reportedly declined, and the backlog there also shrank.

Still Worth Noting

  • Record backlog: Driven by airport and municipal demand. It means a lot of future revenue is lined up, but if costs keep rising, less profit may remain from the same revenue.
  • Stronger balance sheet: Net debt and leverage are both coming down.
  • Further acquisition planned: The O.J. Watson acquisition is scheduled, bringing both business expansion and financial burden.

Share Price and Shareholders

The November 9 closing price was about $11.41, and the market capitalization in early November was around $900 million. The recent 52-week range is about $8.91–15.96. Since the stock fell about 4% on the earnings day, the current price may be lower, so please check real-time quotes yourself. The share price change versus a year ago is -0.27%, essentially flat.

Major shareholders include founding and core holders such as PCS Holding AG (about 24.6%), Gebuka AG (about 13.6%) and Peter Spuhler (about 10.6%). Among asset managers, Pzena (about 5.6%) and T. Rowe Price (about 4.4%) are listed. With large stakes held by major shareholders, the free float is limited, and with median annual trading value of around $2.89 million, trading can be thin. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.025 per share, payable on December 17. Korea's National Pension Service does not hold this stock.

What to Watch Next

  • Whether price increases catch up with cost increases and gross margin recovers
  • Whether weak demand in Europe and other regions continues
  • Whether the accumulated backlog converts into revenue as planned
  • Whether leverage stays at the target level after the acquisition

In short, Aebi Schmidt has piled up work at a record level, but how much profit it can keep from that work is now being tested.
